title: Eagles defeat Titans in thrilling comeback led by Jalen Hurts
seoTitle: Eagles defeat Titans in thrilling comeback led by Hurts
subtitle: Eagles quarterback overcomes two interceptions and answers critics in a tight 24‑20 victory.
excerpt: Jalen Hurts' decisive performance propelled the Philadelphia Eagles to a dramatic 24‑20 win over the Tennessee Titans.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The dramatic 24‑20 victory of the Philadelphia Eagles over the Tennessee Titans last Sunday, driven by a decisive performance from quarterback Jalen Hurts, shook the sports world and sparked great interest in the game results. The matchup, marked by comebacks and pre‑game statements, culminated in an exhilarating final play that secured the Eagles' triumph in Nashville.

The Eagles' comeback and Hurts' performance

The Philadelphia Eagles secured a tight 24‑20 win against the Tennessee Titans in a game that saw quarterback Jalen Hurts lead a decisive drive in the final minutes. Hurts, who overcame two interceptions during the contest, orchestrated a nine‑play, 65‑yard drive in under two minutes. The final play was a three‑yard touchdown pass to Darius Cooper with just nine seconds left on the clock, sealing the score. This victory gave the Eagles a 2‑0 record for the fourth time in five years.

Simmons' controversial remark

The game was preceded by comments from Titans defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who said, "We just need to make Jalen Hurts a quarterback." The remark, which spread quickly, suggested that the key to beating the Eagles would be to limit Hurts' runs and force him into passing situations. After the win, Hurts did not hesitate to address Simmons' comments, indicating that the observation served as extra motivation for his on‑field performance.

The matchup history with Saleh

Beyond Simmons' comments, another motivational factor for Hurts was the history of success by defenses crafted by Robert Saleh, the Titans' current head coach. Saleh, while coaching the 49ers, was responsible for the wild‑card victory over the Eagles last January, where Hurts was limited to 168 yards on 20 of 35 passes. He was also present in the Eagles' loss to the Jets in Week 6 of 2023, when Saleh's defense intercepted Hurts three times, resulting in a 20‑14 Jets win. Hurts mentioned Saleh after the game, saying, "It was good to get him. He posed big challenges, but I kind of crossed that off my list."

Jalen Hurts' journey of overcoming adversity

Although not perfect, with two interceptions, Hurts showed resilience and focus. Titans safety Amani Hooker returned an interception 92 yards for a potential touchdown. However, Hurts led the team in crucial moments, such as a 19‑yard pass to DeVonta Smith on third down and a 20‑yard pass to Dontayvion Wicks at the start of the final drive. Smith, in turn, recorded 117 receiving yards and a touchdown, playing a key role in the winning drive. Hurts' ability to stay calm and believe in himself under pressure was highlighted by teammates like Jordan Mailata, who said, "It's a sense of belief. It's more like a knowing. I know he'll lead us, I know he'll make the right reads, I know he'll throw the right passes."

Impact of the win on the season

The victory not only solidified the Eagles' position as a team to watch early in the season, but also served as a statement from Jalen Hurts about his capability as a quarterback. By overcoming adversity and criticism, he reinforced his reputation as a clutch player. The game, played in heat and humidity in Nashville on Sunday, September 20, 2026, was a test for the squad, which proved superior for most of the first half but needed its quarterback's heroic comeback to secure the positive result.

With information from Inquirer.com, Bleacher Report.
